title: RBI: Notification — Reserve Bank of India (Regional Rural Banks – Know Your Customer) Amendment Directions, 2026
applicability: Regional Rural Banks
description: RBI has issued a notification concerning Reserve Bank of India (Regional Rural Banks – Know Your Customer) Amendment Directions, 2026.
summary: Paragraph 4(1)(v) of the Regional Rural Banks - Know Your Customer Directions, 2025 has been substituted to extend alternative certified copy verification options to Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs). The Reserve Bank reviewed extant instructions and decided to extend this facility to FPIs in addition to Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) and Persons of Indian Origin (PIOs). In practice, compliance workflows for onboarding FPIs will now permit the acceptance of original certified copies issued by specified overseas authorities, branches, or officials rather than requiring direct comparison with originals by the bank in India.
takeaway: Update the KYC verification procedures for Regional Rural Banks to accept original certified copies for Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) certified by the authorized overseas authorities, branches, or officials listed in paragraph 4(1)(v) of the amended directions.

title: RBI: Notification — Reserve Bank of India (Local Area Banks – Know Your Customer) Amendment Directions, 2026
applicability: Local Area Banks dealing with Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs)
description: RBI has issued a notification concerning Reserve Bank of India (Local Area Banks – Know Your Customer) Amendment Directions, 2026.
summary: The Reserve Bank of India has substituted paragraph 4(1)(v) of the Reserve Bank of India (Local Area Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 to extend an alternative verification facility to Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs). This change was made after reviewing extant instructions to allow FPIs, alongside Non-Resident Indians and Persons of Indian Origin, to provide original certified copies of documents certified by specified overseas authorities or officials. In practice, compliance workflows for onboarding FPIs will now accept these alternatively certified documents instead of requiring local comparison with originals by the bank.
takeaway: Update the bank's KYC verification procedures for Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) to accept original certified copies certified by authorized overseas officials, notary publics abroad, court magistrates, judges, or Indian Embassies/Consulates General.

title: RBI: Notification — Reserve Bank of India (Small Finance Banks – Know Your Customer) Amendment Directions, 2026
applicability: Small Finance Banks dealing with Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs)
description: RBI has issued a notification concerning Reserve Bank of India (Small Finance Banks – Know Your Customer) Amendment Directions, 2026.
summary: The Reserve Bank of India has amended paragraph 5(1)(v) of the Reserve Bank of India (Small Finance Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025. This change was introduced to extend the alternative certification facility for customer documents to Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs), following a review of extant instructions. In practice, compliance workflows will now allow small finance banks to accept original certified copies of officially valid documents for FPIs certified by specified overseas authorities, branches, or officials rather than requiring local verification.
takeaway: Update the bank's KYC onboarding procedures for Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) to accept alternatively certified original documents from the specified overseas authorities, branches, or officials.

title: IBBI: Circular — Due diligence by Insolvency Professionals regarding misuse of IBC framework
applicability: All Registered Insolvency Professionals, All Insolvency Professional Entities, and All Insolvency Professional Agencies
description: IBBI has issued a circular concerning Due diligence by Insolvency Professionals regarding misuse of IBC framework.
summary: IBBI has introduced specific due diligence requirements and illustrative indicators for Insolvency Professionals to detect potential misuse of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code framework for purposes other than resolution or liquidation. The regulator issued this circular after receiving information from law enforcement and regulatory agencies regarding cases where the framework was misused to mitigate tax liabilities, close or merge companies without scrutiny, or avoid investigations and penalties. In practice, compliance workflows will require Insolvency Professionals to remain vigilant to six listed illustrative indicators during the CIRP or liquidation process, conduct further holistic enquiries upon noticing them, and apply to the Adjudicating Authority if they form a view that the process serves a fraudulent or malicious purpose.
takeaway: Review the official document to determine applicability and required action.

summary: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI / Board) has received information from law enforcement and regulatory agencies that , in certain cases, the framework under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (Code / IBC) is being misused for purposes other than insolvency resolution or liquidation of the corporate debtor (CD).

Such instances include, inter alia, mitigating tax liabilities, clos ure/merger of companies without regulatory scrutiny, mitigat ing investigations, prosecution and penalties under various statutes, monetising and ring-fencing assets etc.
Insolvency Professionals (IPs) should remain vigilant to circumstances that may indicate misuse of the insolvency process.

title: IBBI: Circular — Extension of time for filing Forms to monitor insolvency resolution processes for Personal Guarantors to Corporate Debtors
applicability: All Registered Insolvency Professionals, All Recognised Insolvency Professional Entities, and All Registered Insolvency Professional Agencies
description: IBBI has issued a circular concerning extension of time for filing Forms to monitor insolvency resolution processes for Personal Guarantors to Corporate Debtors.
summary: The Board has extended the last date for submission of all applicable PGIRP forms (PGIRP-1 to PGIRP-6) to 30th September 2026, alongside shifting the enforcement date for penalties on delayed submissions or modifications to the same date. This extension was granted in response to representations from Insolvency Professionals and Insolvency Professional Agencies citing technicalities, difficulties, and transitional time required to familiarize themselves with the electronic platform. In practice, compliance workflows will allow submissions and corrections without penalty until 30th September 2026, while workflows must also incorporate stricter accuracy checks to prevent the submission of incorrect or incomplete information.
takeaway: Ensure that all PGIRP forms are accurately submitted by the extended deadline of 30th September 2026 to avoid the levying of penalties, and verify that all information entered is truthful and consistent with attached supporting documents rather than using placeholder or zero values.

description: CIRCULAR

Subject: Extension of time for filing Forms to monitor insolvency resolution processes for Personal Guarantors to Corporate Debtors under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, and the regulations made thereunder.
summary: The last date for submission of all applicable PGIRP forms as per paragraph 9 of Circular No. IBBI/II/92/2026 is hereby extended till 30th September 2026.
In line with this extension, penalties for delayed submission or modification of these forms shall now be levied only after 30th September 2026.

representations have been received from Insolvency Professionals (IPs) and Insolvency Professional Agencies (IPAs) requesting an extension of the deadline, citing technicalities, difficulties, and the transitional time required to familiarize themselves with the electronic platform and submission of the forms.
some IPs have been submitting incorrect or incomplete information in electronic forms filed with the Board, such as entering zero values across mandatory fields simply to complete the submission.
takeaway: The last date for submission of all applicable PGIRP forms as per paragraph 9 of Circular No. IBBI/II/92/2026 is hereby extended till 30th September 2026.
penalties for delayed submission or modification of these forms shall now be levied only after 30th September 2026.
IPs shall ensure all information submitted via the PGIRP forms is accurate, truthful, and entirely consistent with the supporting documents attached thereto.
